title: Canonical truncation commutes with pullback on universally free lowest-cohomology charts
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and K a perfect object [def-pc-perfect-complex] of D(O_S) [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume H^i(Lk^*K)=0 for every scheme Y, k:Y→S and i<0, using [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Assume each s∈S has an open neighbourhood U and r∈ℕ such that H^0(L(k≫U.ι)^*K) is finite locally free of rank r [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] for every scheme Y and k:Y→U. Let M be an O_S-module and a:M[0]→K a derived morphism with H^0(a) an isomorphism. Then for every scheme Y and k:Y→S, H^0(Lk^*a) is an isomorphism. This is a statement about the specified derived morphism, not merely existence of an object isomorphism.

source.place: matrix-chart proof and canonical pullback clause; Tags 0BCD, 08CR, 06YD

proof.text: Choose U,r at s and test the universal condition at the residue field of s. In the finite-free residue model the first term has rank r, and all negative terms vanish by the negative fibre hypothesis. Shrink into U and an affine chart.

The identity test makes H0(K) locally free of rank r. Trivialize its inclusion into the first rank-r free term. Its cokernel has zero dual by the square-injective-free-map lemma. Each coordinate of the outgoing differential factors through that cokernel, hence vanishes. Consequently d0=0, including over nonreduced rings.

The H0 isomorphism identifies M with this first free term. On an affine subchart represent a by an actual chain map of bounded finite-free complexes. Its degree-zero component is its H0 map, hence invertible. Termwise pullback computes derived pullback, retains d0=0 and no negative terms, and takes that component to an isomorphism.

Inverse images of the model charts cover Y. Restriction is exact and commutes with derived pullback, so H0(Lk*a) is locally the map just computed. Open-cover detection gives the global isomorphism; rank zero and empty schemes need no exception.

theorem perfect_universalH0_truncation_pullback_isIso
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (S : Scheme.{u})
    [∀ U : S.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory S) (hK : IsPerfect S K)
    (hnegative : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (k : Y ⟶ S) (i : ℤ), i < 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) i).obj
          ((derivedPullback k).obj K)))
    (hloc : ∀ s : S, ∃ U : S.Opens, s ∈ U ∧ ∃ r : ℕ,
      ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (k : Y ⟶ U.toScheme),
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
              ((derivedPullback (k ≫ U.ι)).obj K)) r)
    (M : S.Modules)
    (a : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj M ⟶ K)
    (ha : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) 0).map a))
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (k : Y ⟶ S) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).map
        ((derivedPullback k).map a))
